div.p: There are so many reasons to get to know Saint Anselm College. On our Hilltop, you will find your place, your passions, your direction. Out of all the reasons to attend Saint Anselm, find yours.

section.p: Since 1889, Saint Anselm College has provided a transformative education shaped by Catholic and Benedictine values and a liberal arts foundation. Here, you are part of a welcoming community where you will discover your passions, experience cherished traditions, and unlock your full potential.

section.p: "Saint Anselm College prepares students not simply for careers, but for lives of purpose, leadership, and service. Rooted in our Catholic and Benedictine tradition, we cultivate critical thinkers and compassionate leaders who engage new ideas, respect differing perspectives, and seek the common good. Through a distinctive liberal arts and professional education, Anselmians are prepared to lead and serve a changing world."

p.a: Learn about the College's 12th President

h2.span: In the classroom and in the community, an Anselmian education will challenge you to find your best self.

p.em: Nicole Gugliucci, Ph.D., Department Chair and Associate Professor, Physics, was featured in the most recent issue of Portraits Magazine's Focus on Faculty.

p.span: “Turns out what I like most about science is sharing it with other people. Teaching it, and sharing it with others. … It’s important to me that everyone can feel some connection to science and see that it is understandable, it is reachable, it is even doable.”

img.alt: Book Group Discussion of "The Dream Hotel" on September 24, 2026

span.span: Expand for more info about Book Group Discussion | Thursday, September 26, 2026
Close for less info about Book Group Discussion | Thursday, September 26, 2026

div.p: All members of the Saint Anselm College community are invited to attend a book discussion of "The Dream Hotel" by Laila Lalami.

p.strong: Copies of the book are available to borrow at the Circulation Desk.

div.p:
Date: Thursday, September 24, 2026
Time: 1:00 - 2:00 p.m.
Location: Library Classroom, upper level of Geisel.

p.strong: Attendees are welcome to bring their lunches to the book group meeting.

div.p: "Sara has just landed at LAX, returning home from a conference abroad, when agents from the Risk Assessment Administration pull her aside and inform her that she will soon commit a crime. Using data from her dreams, the RAA’s algorithm has determined that she is at imminent risk of harming the person she loves most: her husband. For his safety, she must be kept under observation for twenty-one days.

Eerie, urgent, and ceaselessly clear-eyed, The Dream Hotel artfully explores the seductive nature of technology, which puts us in shackles even as it makes our lives easier. Lalami asks how much of ourselves must remain private if we are to remain free, and whether even the most invasive forms of surveillance can ever capture who we really are" (Goodreads.com).

p.a: Event details for Book Group Discussion | Thursday, September 26, 2026

img.alt: Artificial Intelligence and Catholic Health Care: Challenges and Opportunities

div.a: Artificial Intelligence and Catholic Health Care: Challenges and Opportunities

span.span: Expand for more info about Artificial Intelligence and Catholic Health Care: Challenges and Opportunities
Close for less info about Artificial Intelligence and Catholic Health Care: Challenges and Opportunities

div.p: Register for this event →

Could artificial intelligence undermine the human-centered approach of Catholic health care? Or could it actually free Catholic clinicians to more faithfully advance the healing ministry of Jesus Christ?

Join Prof. Shaun Slusarski of the Theology Department as he shares his insights from the Catholic Health Association’s March 2026 conference, “Artificial Intelligence, Authentic Mercy: Navigating AI Ethics in Catholic Health”.
Shaun Slusarski is a faculty member in the Theology Department. His research focuses on Catholic social teaching and bioethics.
Register for this event →

p.a: Event details for Artificial Intelligence and Catholic Health Care: Challenges and Opportunities

div.a: Conspirator in Chief: The Long Tradition of Presidential Conspiracy Mongering – Stephen Knott, PhD

span.span: Expand for more info about Conspirator in Chief: The Long Tradition of Presidential Conspiracy Mongering – Stephen Knott, PhD
Close for less info about Conspirator in Chief: The Long Tradition of Presidential Conspiracy Mongering – Stephen Knott, PhD

div.p: Conspiracy theories have been part of American political life from the beginning. Drawing from his recent book, Conspirator in Chief: The Long Tradition of Conspiracy Theories in the American Presidency, Knott examines presidents throughout American history who promoted or circulated political rumors and falsehoods, exploring how such claims have been used to undermine opponents and influence public opinion.

He will offer examples ranging from Thomas Jefferson to Donald Trump, as well as presidents who shunned conspiracy mongering and appealed instead to what Abraham Lincoln called the “better angels of our nature.”
Books may be purchased in advance through online or local booksellers. A book signing will follow.
This event is free and open to the public. No advance registration required.
Bio:

Dr. Stephen Knott is an Emeritus Professor of National Security Affairs at the United States Naval War College in Newport, RI and is the Thomas & Mabel Guy Professor of American History and Government at Ashland University. Prior to accepting his position at the Naval War College, Knott was Co-Chair of the Presidential Oral History Program at the Miller Center of Public Affairs at the University of Virginia. He is the author or co-author of eleven books examining with the American presidency, the early republic, and American foreign policy. His most recent book, Conspirator in Chief: The Long Tradition of Conspiracy Theories in the American Presidency, was published in 2026.

p.a: Event details for Conspirator in Chief: The Long Tradition of Presidential Conspiracy Mongering – Stephen Knott, PhD

span.span: Expand for more info about Frederick Douglass Student Colloquium
Close for less info about Frederick Douglass Student Colloquium

p.span: We invite you to participate in the upcoming Learning Liberty Colloquium, hosted by the Center for Ethics in Society and facilitated by Philosophy Professor Tom Larson.

div.p: This event promises a weekend of thoughtful study, reflection, and engaging conversations about the writings of Frederick Douglass.
Students will read 75-100 pages in preparation for this colloquium and will receive a $150 stipend for their participation.
Food will be provided.

p.a: Event details for Frederick Douglass Student Colloquium
